exposure: Program of prevention and management of obstetric hemorrhage
outcome: Complications (blood loss, need for blood transfusions, anemia in the postpartum period)
cohort: The study included 51 patients who underwent obstetric hysterectomy at the General Hospital Dr. Aurelio Valdivieso in Oaxaca, Mexico, between January 2012 and November 2015.
finding: The prevalence of obstetric hysterectomy was 17.1/10,000, primarily indicated by abnormal placental adhesion and uterine atony, and it was associated with postpartum anemia, with no maternal mortality by massive obstetric hemorrhage in the last four years.
mod_finding: The prevalence of post-cesarean obstetric hysterectomy was 25.6/10,000, while postpartum obstetric hysterectomy (implying after vaginal birth) was 10.6/10,000.
